_comment: Sample scan result fixture. Illustrates the JSON shape returned by GET /scan-results/{id}. Field values are representative — not from a real scan.

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy header is absent. This allows execution of inline scripts and loading of resources from any origin, increasing XSS risk.
findings.remediation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header with a restrictive policy. Start with `default-src 'self'` and expand as needed.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options not set
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options header is missing. The page may be embedded in an iframe by a third-party site, enabling clickjacking attacks.
findings.remediation: Add `X-Frame-Options: DENY` or use a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive.

findings.title: Session cookie missing Secure flag
findings.description: A cookie that appears to be a session identifier does not have the Secure attribute. It may be transmitted over plain HTTP if the user is downgraded.
findings.remediation: Set the Secure attribute on all session and authentication cookies.

findings.title: Cookie missing HttpOnly flag
findings.description: A cookie is accessible to JavaScript. If XSS is present, this cookie could be exfiltrated by attacker-controlled scripts.
findings.remediation: Add the HttpOnly attribute to cookies that do not need to be read by client-side JavaScript.

findings.title: Third-party script loaded from unrecognized CDN
findings.description: A <script> tag loads JavaScript from a third-party domain not in the known-good list. Supply chain compromises via CDNs are an established attack vector.
findings.remediation: Verify the third-party CDN is trusted. Consider self-hosting critical scripts or pinning with Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes.

findings.title: TLS 1.0/1.1 negotiation accepted
findings.description: The server may accept TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 connections. These protocol versions are deprecated and have known weaknesses.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to require TLS 1.2 or 1.3. Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 in your TLS configuration.

findings.title: Server header reveals software version
findings.description: The Server response header includes the server software name and version. This is low-risk but provides information to an attacker performing reconnaissance.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to suppress or generalize the Server header.
